hmmt-feb-2014-geo-01.title: Pythagoras
hmmt-feb-2014-geo-01.body:
Let $O$ be the common center and $M$ the midpoint of $AB$. Then $OM\perp AB$ and $OM=\sqrt{4^2-1^2}=\sqrt{15}$. The line $AB$ meets the circle of radius $6$ in a chord with half-length $CM=\sqrt{6^2-15}=\sqrt{21}$, so $CD=2\sqrt{21}$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt{21}$**

hmmt-feb-2014-geo-02.title: Coordinates
hmmt-feb-2014-geo-02.body:
Put $\ell$ as the $x$-axis, $T=(0,0)$ and $P=(5,12)$ (so $PT=13$). The circle tangent to $\ell$ at $T$ has center $(0,R)$ and radius $R$. Passing through $P$: $5^2+(12-R)^2=R^2$, so $25+144-24R=0$ and $R=\frac{169}{24}$.

**Answer: $\frac{169}{24}$**

hmmt-feb-2014-geo-03.title: An isosceles triangle $ABM$
hmmt-feb-2014-geo-03.body:
The external bisector at $A$ is perpendicular to the internal bisector of $\angle BAC=\angle BAM$. So $BM$ is perpendicular to the bisector of $\angle A$ in triangle $ABM$; a bisector that is also an altitude means $AB=AM$. Hence $AB=AM=\frac12AC=6$.

Then the sides are $6,10,12$ with semiperimeter $14$, and Heron's formula gives $\sqrt{14\cdot8\cdot4\cdot2}=\sqrt{896}=8\sqrt{14}$.

**Answer: $8\sqrt{14}$**

hmmt-feb-2014-geo-04.title: Reflect $B$ across $CD$
hmmt-feb-2014-geo-04.body:
Let $B'$ be the reflection of $B$ across $CD$. Then $CB'=CB=AD$, $\angle CB'D=\angle CBD=82^\circ$ and $\angle DCB'=\angle BCD=70^\circ$.

Since $\angle DAC+\angle CB'D=98^\circ+82^\circ=180^\circ$ and these are opposite angles of $ACB'D$, this quadrilateral is cyclic. In it the sides $AD$ and $CB'$ are equal chords, so it is an isosceles trapezoid with parallel sides $AC$ and $DB'$ and the base angles at $A$ and $C$ are equal: $\angle ACB'=\angle CAD=98^\circ$.

Therefore $\angle ACD=\angle ACB'-\angle DCB'=98^\circ-70^\circ=28^\circ$.

**Answer: $28^\circ$**

hmmt-feb-2014-geo-05.title: Cross-section
hmmt-feb-2014-geo-05.body:
Take the plane through $P$ perpendicular to the $xy$-plane and containing the origin (it contains the point $(3,4,0)$ below $P$). By symmetry the largest sphere has its center in this plane, and its great circle in this plane is the incircle of the cross-section triangle, so the answer is that inradius.

The plane meets the unit circle at $U=(\frac35,\frac45,0)$ and $V=(-\frac35,-\frac45,0)$. The triangle $PUV$ has $UV=2$, $PU=\sqrt{\frac{144+256}{25}+64}=\sqrt{80}=4\sqrt5$, $PV=\sqrt{\frac{324+576}{25}+64}=10$, and area $\frac12\cdot2\cdot8=8$ (the foot of $P$ lies on line $UV$, at height $8$). The inradius is $r=\frac{\text{area}}{s}=\frac{8}{(2+4\sqrt5+10)/2}=\frac{16}{12+4\sqrt5}=\frac{4}{3+\sqrt5}=3-\sqrt5$.

**Answer: $3-\sqrt5$**

hmmt-feb-2014-geo-06.title: Ratio of areas
hmmt-feb-2014-geo-06.body:
$AC=\sqrt{25+36}=\sqrt{61}$. In triangle $ACD$, $61=16+25-2\cdot4\cdot5\cos\angle ADC$, so $\cos\angle ADC=-\frac12$ and $\angle ADC=120^\circ$. Since $E$ lies on $AC$, $\frac{BE}{ED}=\frac{[ABC]}{[ADC]}$ (same base $AC$). $[ABC]=\frac12\cdot5\cdot6=15$ and $[ADC]=\frac12\cdot4\cdot5\sin120^\circ=5\sqrt3$. So $\frac{BE}{ED}=\frac{15}{5\sqrt3}=\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $\sqrt3$**

hmmt-feb-2014-geo-07.title: Similar triangles
hmmt-feb-2014-geo-07.body:
Since $BB'$ is a diameter, $\angle BAB'=90^\circ$, so $AB'\perp AB$; also $OM\perp AB$ ($M$ the midpoint of the chord). So $AB'\parallel OM$, and $OM=\frac12AB'$ (midline of triangle $BAB'$). Triangles $XAB'$ and $XOM$ are similar, so $\frac{AX}{XO}=\frac{AB'}{OM}=2$ and $AX=\frac23AO=\frac23R$.

The circumradius of the $13$-$14$-$15$ triangle (area $84$) is $R=\frac{13\cdot14\cdot15}{4\cdot84}=\frac{65}8$. So $AX=\frac23\cdot\frac{65}{8}=\frac{65}{12}$.

**Answer: $\frac{65}{12}$**

hmmt-feb-2014-geo-08.title: Power of the centroid
hmmt-feb-2014-geo-08.body:
The triangle is right-angled at $A$ ($6^2+8^2=10^2$), so $AN=\frac12BC=5$ and $[ABC]=24$. Let $G=AN\cap CM$ be the centroid: $GA=\frac23\cdot5=\frac{10}3$, and $CM=\sqrt{8^2+3^2}=\sqrt{73}$, so $GM=\frac{\sqrt{73}}3$.

The circle $AMY$ is tangent to line $AN$ at $A$, so by the power of the point $G$: $GM\cdot GY=GA^2$, hence $GY=\frac{100/9}{\sqrt{73}/3}=\frac{100}{3\sqrt{73}}$ ($Y$ lies beyond $M$ on ray $CM$).

Both $[GAM]$ and $[NAY]$ are measured with the same angle $\theta$ between lines $AN$ and $CM$ at $G$: $[GAM]=\frac12GA\cdot GM\sin\theta=\frac16[ABC]=4$ and $[NAY]=\frac12NA\cdot GY\sin\theta$. Dividing, $[NAY]=4\cdot\frac{NA\cdot GY}{GA\cdot GM}=4\cdot\frac{5\cdot\frac{100}{3\sqrt{73}}}{\frac{10}3\cdot\frac{\sqrt{73}}3}=4\cdot\frac{150}{73}=\frac{600}{73}$.

**Answer: $\frac{600}{73}$**

hmmt-feb-2014-geo-09.title: Radical center = incenter
hmmt-feb-2014-geo-09.body:
Let $\omega_i$ have center $O_i$ and radius $r_i$. Orthogonality of $\omega_3$ to $\omega_i$ means the power of $O_3$ with respect to $\omega_i$ is $r_3^2$, for $i=1,2,4$. So $O_3$ is the radical center of $\omega_1,\omega_2,\omega_4$.

These three circles are pairwise externally tangent, so $O_1O_2O_4$ has sides $r_1+r_2$, $r_1+r_4$, $r_2+r_4$, and its incircle touches the sides exactly at the three points of tangency. The common tangent lines at those points are the radical axes, which meet at the incenter $I$, so the radical center is $I$ and its power to each circle is the squared tangent length $\rho^2$, where $\rho$ is the inradius. Hence $r_3^2=\rho^2$. With semiperimeter $s=r_1+r_2+r_4$ and area $\sqrt{s\,r_1r_2r_4}$ (Heron), $\rho^2=\frac{r_1r_2r_4}{r_1+r_2+r_4}$.

So $8=\frac{10\cdot13\cdot r_4}{23+r_4}$, i.e. $184+8r_4=130r_4$ and $r_4=\frac{184}{122}=\frac{92}{61}$.

**Answer: $\frac{92}{61}$**

hmmt-feb-2014-geo-10.title: Monge's theorem
hmmt-feb-2014-geo-10.body:
The foot $D$ of the altitude from $A$ has $BD=5$, $DC=9$, $AD=12$. Let $N$ be the midpoint of $BC$: $BN=7$, $DN=2$. Since $BS-CS=\frac4{15}$, $S$ is on the $C$-side of $N$ with $NS=\frac2{15}$, so $DS=2+\frac2{15}=\frac{32}{15}$.

Let line $AS$ meet line $MN$ (the perpendicular bisector of $BC$, through $O$) at $P$. Since $AD\parallel NP$, $NP=AD\cdot\frac{SN}{SD}=12\cdot\frac{2/15}{32/15}=\frac34$, with $P$ on the same side of $BC$ as $A$ and $O$. The circumradius is $R=\frac{13\cdot14\cdot15}{4\cdot84}=\frac{65}8$ and $ON=\sqrt{R^2-7^2}=\frac{33}8$, so $OP=\frac{33}8-\frac34=\frac{27}8$ and $PM=OM-OP=\frac{65}8-\frac{27}8=\frac{19}4$.

By Monge's theorem for the circles $\omega_1,\omega_2,\Gamma$: the exsimilicenter of $\omega_1$ and $\Gamma$ (which is $A$), the insimilicenter of $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ (which is $T$), and the insimilicenter $P'$ of $\omega_2$ and $\Gamma$ are collinear. The insimilicenter $P'$ lies on the line of centers $OM$, so $P'=AT\cap OM=P$. It divides $OM$ in the ratio of the radii: $\frac{\rho}{R}=\frac{MP}{OP}=\frac{19/4}{27/8}=\frac{38}{27}$, so $\rho=\frac{65}8\cdot\frac{38}{27}=\frac{1235}{108}$.

**Answer: $\frac{1235}{108}$**
